tips.comment: Been following him for a while. He has been touted for better things. One worry is that he has been withdrawn a couple of times, so is he fit? His reputation says he is worth a punt.
Ran well on debut when 4th. Was short of room but stayed on well over 7f. Step up in trip will suit, and with improvement likely, shouldn't be far away.

Archivist has a lot of 2s in his form line, but is likely to find a bit for his seasonal return at Nottingham last month. He stays at a mile for now, although he had been entered over 10 furlongs in an 8k maiden at Doncaster (non-runner - off feed). Charlie Johnston's yard is just starting to move up a gear now, after a slow start, so an each-way angle into this race is Clouds Hill. A Cracksman colt, he was a good 1.25L second at Musselburgh over 8 furlongs when weak in the market beforehand. He should have learned a lot from that and will appreciate more of a stamina test at Leicester.
Jack Channon's three-year-old newcomer Brave Guest obviously could be anything, but I like this combo. So again, a small stake each way. Watch the market for clues.

Beaten favorite last time at Ayr when backed into 7/4 but had to settle for 2nd after never settling and then hitting the front too early. Runs off the same handicap mark today and an eye-catching jockey booking of Tom Marquand.
Chalk Mountain is yet to win on turf, although it has won five times on the all-weather surface. He was third in his last run, beaten just over a length off. Looks ready to break his turf duck.

There is rain due this morning at Leicester, and any softening of the ground will suit Liamarty Dream. He wasn't disgraced at Chester two starts ago in a higher grade than this. He drops in grade and could potentially be back on ground with a bit of cut, and I think that will really suit. His last win came off 88, and he's now down to 81. He's very well handicapped and should go well if the rain gets into the ground.

MANHATTAN MIRAGE appears to be on a workable looking opening handicap mark and he has been given time along with plenty of experience through qualifying. He has shown up well when fresh previously , so with the yard among the winners and Rossa Ryan booked there are reasons to be hopeful.
Stable in good form. Wears cheekpieces for the first time and looks to be on a fairly lenient mark for his handicap debut.
An unexposed horse over this distance. Value looking price with plenty of support in the market. A good 2nd last time out and cheekpieces on that could help. A solid chance.

Not the most reliable, Emily Rebecca disappointed last time in first blinkers at Chepstow after being slow away. She had previously finished in 2nd place in her other two races this season. Dropped back a pound and with the blinkers off again, she could go close under Joe Leavy for Richard Hannon's stable.

Finally this horse gets the step up in trip that he's been absolutely crying out for and he is a strong bet for me here from a good draw. The horse is nearly always slowly away and outpaced before making up ground late on when the winners have flown. This extra trip is therefore going to be ideal and clearly something has clicked with this jockey lately since he's riding out of his skin at the moment for his red hot trainer and he looks worthy of a bet here for sure.

This is a class six affair, and only one of these knows what it's actually like to win a race. So maybe CUDA BEEN A ROWLEX can outrun this price and shake off a couple of disappointing runs with the new headgear. The stable is in form and does particularly well over these sorts of middle distances, so it is worth each-way consideration.

Aurelius Maximus is set to compete in the 14:47 at Leicester tomorrow, a Class 6 apprentice handicap over 1m 2f. Trained by Ed Dunlop and ridden by apprentice Mason Patel, who claims a valuable 7lb, this three-year-old gelding is seeking to build upon his recent performances. 
In his latest outing on 29 April 2025 at Brighton, Aurelius Maximus finished fifth in a Class 6 handicap over 1m 1f 207y, beaten by 4¾ lengths. Prior to that, he was seventh at Redcar on 7 April 2025 over 1m 2f 1y, indicating a level of consistency in his performances. 
The application of Mason Patel's 7lb claim effectively reduces Aurelius Maximus's weight, potentially enhancing his competitiveness in this field. The step back up in trip to 1m 2f could also play to his strengths, providing an opportunity to utilize his stamina. 
Given these factors, Aurelius Maximus presents as a viable each-way option for those seeking value in this contest.

Some quite exposed low-rated horses in this race and also one or two lightly-raced types. Of the second category, Split Silk is quite interesting. She's a 70k Ghaiyyath filly who has only had five runs; two in handicaps. One would think connections will be looking at broodmare potential further down the line, but she will need to win a race or two. 10 furlongs shouldn't be a problem especially with an ease in grade. A positive start should make all the difference. Late foaled, Dance No More might improve for her turf debut last month at Haydock.

Eleven horses contest this race with four making their race course debut. Of those with previous experience only Project Incheon has managed to make the frame when finishing third at Redcar. He finished that race well and is up in trip today. Every possibility he will improve for both that run and a slightly longer trip. If so, he looks to be a major player.
Missed break on debut and never got into the race. Will strip fitter for that run, and the extra furlong will suit. Stable in form, top jockey up.

The two races that Telling Time and Lamnol ran in last time are working out really well in terms of next time out winners and places. Lamnol's class 2 race at this track produced Italica third in the Lily Agnes at Chester and a couple of good winners in high-value maidens. The step up to 7 furlongs is a bit of a question mark, but there is sufficient stamina on the dam's side up to a mile. Application of a hood should be helpful and past track experience a positive too.
This horse was bred for the trip, has a top sire and dam. Could be a contender if the family genes are anything to go by. Intriguing potential.
Torbay from the in-form E Lavelle yard broke free before its last race and then finished nowhere. I'll scrape some shrapnel up for a tiny each way now under Eddie Greatrex.

Jack The Tooth, a 2-year-old bay gelding trained by George Scott. It's always good to have had racecourse experience in this type of race, and out of the 2 horses who have run, Jack The Tooth performed the best, making him the tip.
Only 2 in this field have any experience. Showed glimpses of promise when finishing 8th of 11 on debut and with improvement likely holds an each way chance.

3yo handicap and quite a competitive one for a Class 5. Rossa Ryan (SR 17%) replaces Saffie Osborne on Miss Show Down here, Clive Cox trained filly by Showcasing who looked like she would come on for her seasonal debut in a Class 4 at Goodwood last time (little supported in the market at 22-1). She kept on really well to finish fourth there, having been slowly away and outpaced early. Popular choice for bettors today (best backed horse in the race so far). Decent form in fillies' maidens included a second last year and was a 16-1 winner on her first handicap start. Has lots of potential (to be honest, I'm not sure today will be the day but, on the other hand, it's quite possible).

Rogue Bullet is set to contest the 17:47 at Leicester tomorrow??'a Class 5 handicap over 5 furlongs??'and he presents as a compelling each-way proposition in this 9-runner field. 
Trained by Jack Jones and owned by The Rogues Gallery, this three-year-old gelding has demonstrated consistent form in recent outings. Notably, he secured a victory at Brighton on 12 April 2025 in a Class 5 handicap over 5 furlongs and 215 yards, showcasing his potential when conditions suit. In his most recent race on 14 May 2025 at Yarmouth, Rogue Bullet finished fourth in a Class 5 handicap over 5 furlongs and 42 yards, beaten by 4¼ lengths. Prior to that, he was fifth at Ripon on 26 April 2025 over 6 furlongs, indicating a level of consistency in his performances. These form figures suggest he has the ability to be competitive at this level. 
The return to a straight 5-furlong course at Leicester should play to his strengths, allowing him to utilize his early speed effectively. With a manageable field of nine runners, he should have the opportunity to secure a favorable position early on.
Slow to start, finished 3 lengths behind off a mark of 75 at Wolverhampton last time; typically held up back after a break. Serious contender.

Invincible Crown's last win came in October on the all-weather off a mark of 71 (beat Toolatetonegotiate 1.25L giving her over a stone) then sold for 22k. Since then, he has come back down in the weights from a high of 78. Showed a bit more promise last time at Yarmouth, dropped down into class 5 company. On a fair mark and should be competitive.

Pont Neuf is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Eve Johnson Houghton (landed a 20-1 winner yesterday). He won his first two races as a 2-year-old and opened on a mark of 88. He is a two-time winner over 5f and has been given a chance by the handicapper, having been dropped 4lb from the last run. He makes a second attempt in a class 5 handicap off just 71, so clearly well handicapped. He has posted RPR of 79-77 in class 4 handicaps in the last six starts, so retains some ability. With the application of first-time blinkers, we could see some improvement. He looks to be a value bet at 16-1 under Rhys Clutterbuck in today's grade.
Pastoral Way 3 year old chestnut gelding. Joint bottom weight here, he looks the one to beat. Ran well in a handicap last time out.

Trained by D P Quinn and ridden by Darragh Keenan, this four-year-old gelding has shown flashes of form that suggest he could be competitive here. Notably, he secured a victory at Yarmouth on 30 July 2024 in a Class 6 handicap over 5 furlongs and 42 yards, demonstrating his potential when conditions suit. In his most recent outing on 8 May 2025 at Brighton, Battleofbaltimore finished fifth in a Class 6 handicap over 5 furlongs and 60 yards, beaten by 6 lengths. Prior to that, he had a third-place finish at Brighton on 17 September 2024, indicating his capability over similar distances. His form figures suggest he has the ability to be competitive at this level.

The IMA Architects Classified Stakes (Class 6) features some very low-rated three-year-olds, with prize money of £3,200. Among them, Richard Hammond's filly, Fregola, looks an interesting contender despite her modest rating of 44 and a winless record from ten starts. She returned this season after six months off and has shown slight improvement, particularly at Redcar, where she caught the eye. Last time out, there was market support for her, backed into 9/2 - her shortest price to date - before finishing fourth. She was held up and found herself trapped in a pocket two furlongs out, yet finished strongly under Tyrese Cameron, leaving the impression she had more to give. While this is a low-level contest, a more galloping track should suit her, bringing stamina into play. With the filly's allowance and a 7lb claim against a weak field, she looks well positioned to challenge. Given the stable's strong form, she should be an attractive price and could take some stopping.

Last win at Ripon last August, but in truth, has not looked close to winning since. However, he does have ability, and when in the right mood, is difficult to beat. Conditions tomorrow should suit him.
Secured a tight victory in a handicap off a rating of 74 over 1m2f at Newcastle last outing. Longer distances raise some doubts. Still a key contender.

Just An Hour won well first time out at Nottingham this season, but after being put up six pounds, he could only finish a poor 3rd of 5 next time at Salisbury. Down a pound and trying twelve furlongs for the first time this season, he could go close again.
Pulled out of a race last week because the going didn't suit. Second last time, but should make amends this time around and will be there at the closing stages. Nap win at 4/1.

Weakened a furlong out over this trip in a Class 4 at Doncaster last month and will come on for that run following an absence from the track of 218 days. Drops in grade to Class 5 and Rossa Ryan looks a positive booking in the saddle.

Not totally convinced. Favourite Flickering Halo looks the type to follow up his recent win on the all-weather at Newcastle (landed a bit of a touch). Lincoln Rockstar had a highly successful season last year, winning five times as she defied the handicapper, including over the course and distance. She was stone cold in the market last time at Ripon, and possibly it was not her day, as she was slowly away and disappointing. She is on a winning mark and Marco Ghiani is booked to ride. He rode four of her victories last year and hopefully she bounces back.

Delpotro followed up a couple of good runs by winning last time at Sedgefield. He was probably a bit lucky that day but still looks to be improving. The man of the moment, Bowen, is on top and could follow up.
Dual CD winner and only raised 1 lb for 2 lengths second of 5 in higher grade here 2 weeks ago. Finished behind Duke of Buckley, a horse in fine form.

The model I run suggests Jaitropaclasse can win this one. Jaitropaclasse lines up here with a comparable RPR. All runners in this 6-horse race have a very similar PRR rating. Jaitropaclasse does have the lowest official ranking by a considerable margin and so goes out carrying 6 lbs less than the current market leader and 10 lbs less to the top weight. Charlie Price on board relieves a further 3 lbs, which helps, and takes the total weight differential to nearly a stone on some of these other horses. Comes here in recent form after a good second 17 days ago, so has race fitness. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Two-time course and distance winner Neigh Botha seemed to have hit a flat spot when a 21L 5th of six at Stratford, but before that, he ran a 2.75L second off a pound lower, 12L ahead of the third, at Bangor. He's had a few scratched entries since the Stratford run, so I think the stable have him ready. Could be an across-the-card double.
Was a winner for the first time over fences when winning at Sedgefield in April and followed that with a respectable 3rd at Hexham. Each way chance if in the same form.

Debut chase run. Normally from hurdles to chase, with top trainer, a win is on the cards after hurdle win. Horse finished 3rd, has since won twice, including a class 2 event on good ground at further trip.

Ali Star Bert won off a 102 in March and returned from a short break PU. But that was when stepping up in trip to 3m5f. I think the return to 2m2f could see him bounce back, especially with the overnight rain. and running off a 101 today.

The model I run suggests Zucayan can win this one. Zucayan lines up here with the second highest RPR of this 7-runner field. Comes here in good form after a solid first last time out 23 days ago and looks to carry the same kind of form into this one. Does go out with the second highest official ranking, so carries the second highest weight, but Nick Slatter on board relieves a handy 5 lbs, bringing the total weight being carried more in line with the middle rankings. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Senator has won on both flat and over the hurdles. His last run was at Fakenham, where he showed great fighting qualities to battle back and win after being headed before the last. Could win again.

Max Of Stars has had a few runs over hurdles that were on ground softer than ideal and in better class races than today's, and his mark has dropped 10 lb. Had wind surgery in April before a spin on the flat three weeks ago, 1m4f good, where he shaped well and stayed on late. The 5-year-old has been in the first two 8/11 times over hurdles when on good ground at this trip.
Was a winner at Market Rasen on debut in June last year but has been unable to build on that in 4 races since. Off since December but has an each-way chance if rediscovering that debut form.

Won at Wetherby over 3m in March and did the double when winning here over today's course and distance. 2nd LTO but staying on well over a shorter trip. Back up to 3m today back here and should take some beating.
Ran keenly, placing fourth, 20 lengths off the pace in a Ffos Las handicap last time, but performed well. Expected to improve from the outing.

Reverts back to hurdles for the first time in a while. Was placed here over course and distance off a 6lb higher mark two starts ago when chasing. Only beaten 3 lenghts, So if taking well to the smaller obstacles, he looks to have a cracking chance off a lower mark than his chase mark. Solid each way at least.

The model I run suggests Fantomas can cause an upset here. Not fancied by the early market but 15s represents good value according to the output. This model result has been driven by Fantomas having the highest RPR of the 13 runner field but an official ranking leaving him very well treated in the weights. This means Fantomas goes out carrying nearly 2 stone (!) difference to the current market leader and top weight Aazza. Model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator for this, which translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

Zoffalee returned from almost two years off four weeks ago over hurdles, and it was pleasing to see him run so well for so far in the race, eventually a lack of fitness telling. He will be sharper today, and the three-time hurdle winner is now very well handicapped. He gets this trip and ground and has gained three seconds and a third at this course from four runs here. Worth a go at the price that he is ready to go.

A chance is taken on Global Assembly, who has shown absolutely nothing in all four runs since moving over from Ireland to be based in the UK. All his races in Ireland and here have been over the larger obstacles. Today, following wind surgery, he is entered into his first hurdle race. His last chase race was off a mark of ninety-five, having started as high as one hundred and nine. Over hurdles, his mark is five pounds less on ninety. Hopefully, the combination of wind surgery and hurdling will breathe new life into this eight-year-old.

The model I run suggests Hard Market can win this one. Hard Market lines up here with the highest RPR of this larger 9-horse race and is not overly punished for it in the weights. Hard Market hasn't run too much recently, but a reasonable 4th 58 days ago is some of the better form to go by in this inexperienced race. Tries the tongue tie for the first time to aid concentration. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Tim Easterby is not a name usually associated with bumper winners but he does okay and he has got a good record with the family of Rosie Baloo. She has a very nice pedigree being by the fast up and coming national hunt sire Jack Hobbs and out of the good winner producing mare Tarabaloo who is by Kayf Tara. She wouldn't need to be anything special to win this race.
Has every chance here to land a victory. His form stands up well to this race, and it will be a disappointment if he doesn't take this race.

The model I run suggests Don Virginia can win this one. Don Virginia lines up with the highest RPR of this slightly larger 10-horse race, but isn't impacted too much in the weights. All horses bar 2 go out carrying the same initial amount around this 2m 4f trip. Comes here in decent form and showed a good display to come second 21 days ago. Race fitness should not be a concern and looks to go one better here today. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

First run for experienced trainers, and comes here on the back of a British Point win. Expecting a bit more here, and comes up against horses at the top end of the market that haven't had much success or experience around the larger obstacles yet. Interesting.

Me Tarzan could be worth a shot as he won last time by nearly 4L, which makes me think he can defy the penalty. While there is no money in the bet, he could be a decent end-of-day multiplier in a Lucky 15.

Me Tarzan is the 1/2 favourite here, and this horse got within a length of him at Yarmouth and has an 8lb pull now. In addition to that, the drop back to 7 furlongs favours this horse, and the trainer's runners are going better now than they were when that race was run. The horse's best 3 runs to date were all when the horse finished 4th, and all 3 were the only 3 times that Shoemark has ridden her. She's down to a career-low handicap mark now and is surely the e/w value at 10/1.
Another Abbot just lost out by a head when 2nd at Redcar 8 days ago. Off the same mark of 68, he should lose his maiden tag.
Won his last race by a neck from Sandscreendelivered from a different draw, course, and distance on good to firm. Good jockey on board and should follow up. Great each-way chance at 13/2.
Just lost out to Ghost Man two weeks ago over course and distance but has a more favorable draw and looks unexposed over this shorter distance. Very good chance.

No surprise to see the money coming now that she is dropped back to 5f on quick turf. Those were the conditions that she won under at Nottingham last year in a race that suggests her current mark of 72 is well within her capabilities. Made all the running that day and has the draw closest to the stands rail.

Currently struggling for form but hoping experience over C&D does the trick, as 4 of her last 5 runs have been at this course. But the barren run continues, as it's now been 11 runs since the last win last year. Hoping a lower mark provides the breakthrough.
Beckfords Folly. 2-year-old with the all-conquering Charlie Appleby's stable. The stable's 2-year-olds are running really well this season, and I would expect another winning debutant here.
Daretobedifferent probably showed up best of those that have already run when 3rd behind another Charlie Appleby winning two year old and could go close here at Lingfield.

Tatmeen was unplaced in his first three starts before improving to finish second here, beaten a neck over 8 furlongs in April on his handicap debut. He then stepped up to 12 furlongs at Kempton last month, finishing strongly to win going away by 1 length. He is up 5 lbs here but must have a great chance of following up.
After a win and a second at Windsor in September and October, Artavian came out and ran a good third at Wolverhampton in April. He's proven over the distance and should be fitter for that first run.

Located at the bottom third of the handicap mark in this field but gained valuable experience winning here at a shorter distance back in 2023. The last win was off a higher mark. A bit overpriced in my opinion.

Tourist is a bit inconsistent, but after winning his final race last season at Windsor and his first race this season at Bath, he found the rise from 78 at Windsor up to 86 at Southwell last time too much, and he could only finish 7th. Back to 85 at Lingfield and drawn on the stands side, he could come out on top again against two last-time-out winners also up in the weights.
Not great at Thirsk, and I think this has knocked his price a bit. He runs much better on the all weather and his trainer is in form. Consistent and can do well here at Lingfield.

Has shaped better than the bare result in recent efforts and should be suited by conditions here today. Booking of Hollie Doyle is interesting and now below the last winning mark. Shouldn't be priced as the outsider of the field.
Glamorous Breeze normally takes a run or two to get up to speed after a break and was a surprise winner on the return last month. Although up 4 lbs for that, I would expect more now second up.

Sent off favourite over 2 miles at Wolverhampton 15 days ago but pulled up when his saddle slipped. Connections will be looking to recoup their losses and the drop back to a mile and a half can aid that cause with David Egan also looking a positive jockey booking.

Uther Pendragon has not won for a while now but was not bad when last in a classified back in January. He also did well when fourth when last on Polytrack way back when. But I think more is expected today with the booking of Holly Doyle each way.

Race 2 at Lingfield today is a Conditions Race (Class 6) for 3-year-olds and upwards over 2,414 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the rank outsider Its Life from the W. G. M. Turner yard, and will be ridden by Gina Mangan. This 3-year-old filly is a daughter of Without Parole and has yet to place in 6 starts to date. Her latest was a little frustrating as it was her 3rd run after a rest, and in her previous two runs, she showed definite signs of improvement. Furthermore, she has run to stronger and comparing her form to most of this field, she actually looks to have a good chance of being a challenger for top honors here. Worth keeping an eye on today.

Deep Water Bay is very much a pick on pedigree. Sir Mark Prescott is a master of races like this and has managed a positive ROI from 200 runners, which is extremely rare. This seems to have the right ingredients to get off the mark now upped in trip. Nap for me.

Five starts for the 3yo filly, two runs this year, still unexposed. She was 5th three weeks ago after stepping up to this 12f trip, which was her second start in 2023, beaten 3L but seeing the race out. The 1st and 3rd from that race have run well since, so the form is standing up. Every chance in this weak-looking handicap.
Won an impressive handicap last time out, up in trip here today. Clearly the form horse and one to beat. Enjoys front running and can make it five out of five if he hits the front early.

Ran on inside the final furlong when runner-up over course and distance when last seen on the 22nd of May. Behind an odds-on favourite in that race and remains on the same mark to have every chance of going one better for this 5-time course and distance winner.

Just five career runs for 3yo filly, solid efforts in her two runs this year. Beaten just over a length at this track four weeks ago in a novice stakes, not the best position turning in that day and a little short of room, but saw the race out well. Room for improvement and this slightly longer trip can suit her. These handicap rivals are not as strong as what she faced in her last race.

Failed to land the hat trick of wins when 7th over course and distance, but had to challenge far too wide of the home bend and then got a slight nudge at a crucial stage, and his chance was gone. Good chance to resume winning ways in this race.

Second last time too, Romantic Spirit was clear of the rest. Should turn the tables this time around. Good jockey and trainer at this course. Should be there at the business end of the race. Great each-way bet at 6/1.

Lhebayeb returned from a break in March to two wins, with the second of those being by a bigger margin when stepping up to C5 with the fillies. However, she was not so good last time out when back with the boys. She is worth another shot now back with the fillies.

Just three starts for the 3yo - last Aug/Sept. Not showing a lot but he did run in a couple of good quality novice stake races. Improvement possible after 8 months off the track. Looking at the runners around him in those races his opening handicap mark of 55 is very attractive, plus 5lb taken off by the claiming jockey. He faces four poor looking rivals who are all looking exposed.
In good form having won three of his last five races. Won over course and distance in February. The 2 lbs increase for his latest win doesn't look enough to stop him going in again here.

All 5 career wins for Pessoa have come here, with one of those over course and distance off today's mark of 58 back in February 2023. Drops in trip after just failing when beat a nose over a furlong further here last month and Taryn Langley in the saddle takes a 7 pound allowance which could prove to be valuable.

I think the trip is key to River Alwen's chances in this contest. The fact that he ran well at this venue at the back end of April indicates a horse in relatively good health. We should at least be able to eke out some place money.

Struggling for wins, just only 2 wins from 19 runs to date. Crucially, he is a course winner and now operating 3lbs higher than the last winning mark. 3 of the last 4 runs have been here, and going down in trip should make life a little easier.

Royal Observatory won over course and distance last time when tried in blinkers for the first time. If continuing that improvement here tonight, even with a 3lb penalty for that success, could still be involved in the finish again.

This horse unsurprisingly faded in the final furlong or so last time out when having used up too much juice by having to race wide. The drop back in trip will suit here, and the same jockey can get some compensation with hopefully giving the horse a better ride here. She's well-bred and thoroughly unexposed, so looks worthy of interest at what appears to be a generous price.

Masterofgreygoose was ridden like they didn't care, way back in mid-division in an amateur's race before it ran on looking menacing, before it was squashed up and that was that! Trainer Joseph Parr hasn't won for a while, but he does pretty well here at 16% and has enlisted an in-form good jockey in Benoit d l Sayette, which looks interesting. EW.

Stepping back in trip from 7f to 6f. Looks a good move after the horse didn't see out the 7f trip last time. Drops 1lb also which can only help and looks to have a solid each way chance. Good stall draw in 1.
Remarkably consistent recently - hasn't finished outside the top four in the last ten runs, including two wins in that spell.
Becomimg a bit frustrating but only out of the first four once in five attempts when racing over 7f +. Its a weak class 6 event and he should, at the very least, make the frame.
A distance winner. Was 5th of 9 over course and distance 12 days ago. Drops 1lb for that run so runs off 59. Good draw in 2 so can get a good early position. Solid each way chance.

The last race of the day in England today is Race 6 at Wolverhampton, which is a tricky event with most of the runners having some sort of claim for winning. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old filly Star of Atlantis from the Adrian Wintle yard, and will be ridden by George Wood. This daughter of Starspangledbanner is in good form and won her most recent race here at this course. She could easily follow up on that win for a quickfire double in this field.

Triggered is a course and distance winner, though its last win was back in the 2022/23 season. It has been running consistently well without winning. It was second here last time over course and distance with Luke Morris on board. Hopefully, with luck in running, it will be involved in the finish again.

In his most recent outing on 21 May 2025 at Brighton, Thanks Dad finished fourth in a Class 6 handicap over 7 furlongs and 216 yards, beaten by 3 lengths. Prior to that, he was fourth at Brighton on 30 April 2025 over the same distance, indicating a level of consistency in his performances. Notably, he secured a victory at Southwell on 28 March 2025 in a Class 6 handicap over 7 furlongs and 14 yards, demonstrating his potential when conditions suit. His form figures suggest he has the ability to be competitive at this level. 
The return to Wolverhampton's Tapeta surface, where he has previously performed well, could play to his strengths. With Kieran O'Neill booked to ride, his experience could prove invaluable in navigating the course.

8 lbs below last winning mark and is a much better performer on the AW as opposed to turf. I can forgive a poor run on turf LTO over a distance slightly too far. Interestingly, today the stable has opted to sport the first-time blinkers, having previously been successful with first-time tongue tie and then running 2nd, not beaten far when rocking the Visor TT combo. The fancied horses all have high draws to contend with, and they may get stuck out wide all the way. We're nicely berthed in 3, and hoping the blinkers make a difference today for a stable that can get one ready and usually at decent odds.
